newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX volatilities rise on spot weakness.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX volatilities rise on spot weakness.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options were higher in early afternoon trade on Wednesday as the U.S. dollar lost ground against most major currencies.
"Most people are trying to deal with spot movements," an over-the-counter dealer said.
The U.S. dollar dropped sharply after U.S. stocks sold off. Weakness in stocks then boosted some European currencies, in particular the Swiss franc, which further pressured spot.
Dealers said there was interest on both sides of the market but that trade was light overall.
"The front end remains bid because nobody wants to be caught short gamma in an illiquid and fast-moving market," noted Ted Voorhees, senior trader at Deutsche Bank.
As a result, the volatility curves for dollar/mark, dollar/Swiss and dollar/sterling are close to flat, he said.
Gamma measures the rate of change of an option's delta. Delta, in turn, measures the change in the cost of an option as the price of the underlying contract fluctuates.

Traders profit from long gamma positions by holding short-dated options whenever there is strong volatility movement. Conversely, they are reluctant to be short gamma during periods of high event risk, or volatility.
Voorhees said he expects the front end of the dollar/mark volatility curve to remain bid as a result but said back-end volatility may slip as the dollar steadies.
However, another dealer stressed that the market remains extremely uncertain as to near-term dollar direction.

"I don't think people have any clue what to do. The Fed doesn't look like it's going to raise rates, the U.S. economy looks weak, the trade numbers were not good. There are a lot of reasons to look for the dollar to go down. At the same time, in terms of what's going on in Europe, there are a lot of reasons for the dollar to stay supported," he said.
As a result of this confusion, he said he does not expect volatilities to slide.
At 1230 CST/1830 GMT, implied volatility for one-month dollar/mark at-the-money options was up 0.15 percentage point from the U.S. open at 8.6/8.9 percent, dealers said.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/yen was up 0.05 percentage point at 7.15/7.45 percent.
